title: vender, -er/-ir key sound e, feminine endings, -ity → -idad, me lo / nos lo

cards.title: Recap: -ar verbs
cards.body: Key vowel a: -a (he/she/it/formal you), -an (they / you all), -as (you informal).

cards.title: vender = to sell
cards.body: Think 'vending machine' or 'street vendor'. -er and -ir verbs use e as their key sound.

cards.title: Who does what? Two separate thoughts
cards.body: First work out the verb (who's doing it: vendo), then the object (them: los). Keeping the two thoughts apart stops you mixing up 'she has them' and 'they have her'.
cards.caveat: Use las for feminine things too, not only for women.

cards.title: Feminine endings: -a, -ión
cards.body: Gender belongs to the word. Words ending in -a are mostly feminine (with a few exceptions). Words ending in -ión are always feminine.

cards.title: -ity → -idad (feminine)
cards.body: English -ity usually becomes -idad, which is always feminine.

cards.title: Guess the related word
cards.body: From an -idad word you can guess the adjective: drop -idad and make it sound Spanish. Adjectives change for gender and number: generoso, generosa, generosos, generosas.
cards.caveat: Guesses can be off (common is común, not 'comuno'): that feedback is how you learn.

cards.title: persona, sincero
cards.body: Persona is a feminine word even when it refers to a man. Listening a lot builds the intuition for good guesses.

cards.title: -er/-ir: -e, -en, -es
cards.body: Same pattern as -ar verbs, but with e as the key vowel.

cards.title: me lo: the person comes first
cards.body: Spanish says 'they sell me it'. When two little words come together, the one for the person (me, nos) goes first.

examples.en: Why don't they sell it to me?

cards.title: nos = us
cards.body: Algo isn't one of the little words, so it comes after the verb.

examples.en: They're not selling it to us.

practice.why: vender → vendo; lo before the verb.
-en for they; no lo before the verb.

practice.en: Why don't they sell it to us?
es: Por qué no nos lo venden

practice.why: nos before the verb; algo after.
